evals.prompt: Do a systematic literature review on diffusion models in computer vision. 10 papers, last 2 years, category cs.CV, APA format. Save to default output location.
evals.expected_output: A structured SLR report saved to /mnt/user-data/outputs/ with APA citations, thematic synthesis across 10 papers, and per-paper annotations.
expectations: The skill read SKILL.md for systematic-literature-review
When scholarflow-academic_search_literature was available it was called exactly once with a concise query and year filters; otherwise arxiv_search.py was called exactly once with a 2-3 word query
The arXiv fallback, if used, included --category cs.CV and --sort-by relevance rather than submittedDate
Metadata extraction was delegated via the task tool to subagents, not done inline or via python -c
The APA template file (templates/apa.md) was read
The final report was saved to /mnt/user-data/outputs/ with a filename matching slr-<topic-slug>-<YYYYMMDD>.md
The present_files tool was called to make the report visible to the user
The report contains an Executive Summary section
The report identifies at least 3 themes with cross-paper analysis
The report contains a Convergences and Disagreements section
The report contains a Gaps and Open Questions section
The report contains per-paper annotations for each of the 10 papers
The references section uses APA 7th format, prefers venue plus DOI for published records, and uses arXiv URLs only for preprints
When ScholarFlow was used, the methodology reports successful or failed providers and deduplication counts

evals.prompt: Survey recent papers on graph neural networks for drug discovery. 5 papers, BibTeX format.
evals.expected_output: A structured SLR report with BibTeX citations using @misc entries for arXiv preprints.
expectations: The skill read SKILL.md for systematic-literature-review
ScholarFlow multi-source search was called once when available; otherwise the arXiv fallback was called once with a short query
Metadata extraction was delegated via the task tool to subagents
The BibTeX template file (templates/bibtex.md) was read, not apa.md or ieee.md
The final report was saved to /mnt/user-data/outputs/
The present_files tool was called
ArXiv-only records use @misc while published records with venue and DOI use an appropriate published entry type
ArXiv entries contain eprint and archivePrefix; primaryClass is included only when category metadata is available
The report contains thematic synthesis, not just a list of papers

evals.prompt: Review the literature on retrieval-augmented generation — key findings, limitations, and open questions. 15 papers, IEEE format.
evals.expected_output: A structured SLR report with IEEE numeric citations and 15 papers extracted in parallel batches.
expectations: The skill read SKILL.md for systematic-literature-review
Exactly one retrieval path was used: ScholarFlow with max_results 15 when available, otherwise arxiv_search.py with --max-results 15
Metadata extraction used the task tool with multiple subagent batches (15 papers requires 3 batches of 5)
The IEEE template file (templates/ieee.md) was read
The report uses IEEE numeric citations [1], [2], etc. in the text
The references section uses IEEE format with numbered entries
The report contains per-paper annotations for all papers
The report identifies themes across the papers

evals.expected_output: The SLR skill should NOT be triggered. The request should route to academic-paper-review instead.
expectations: The systematic-literature-review skill was NOT triggered
The agent did not call scholarflow-academic_search_literature or arxiv_search.py
The agent recognized this as a single-paper review request

evals.prompt: What does the literature say about RLHF?
evals.expected_output: The SLR skill should be triggered despite no explicit 'systematic' or 'survey' keyword, because 'the literature' implies multi-paper synthesis.
expectations: The skill read SKILL.md for systematic-literature-review
After resolving scope, the agent used ScholarFlow once when available or the arXiv fallback once
The agent asked a clarification question about scope (paper count, format) or used reasonable defaults
The final output is a multi-paper synthesis, not a single factual answer

evals.prompt: Survey 12 recent papers on GNSS spoofing detection for UAV navigation. Use every configured academic index and APA format, and explain the search coverage.
evals.expected_output: An evidence-oriented SLR whose methodology exposes source coverage, deduplication, degraded providers, and any abstract-related exclusions.
expectations: The skill read SKILL.md for systematic-literature-review
When available, scholarflow-academic_search_literature was called exactly once without an explicit providers restriction
The report names each successful and failed provider using provider_status instead of claiming universal coverage
The methodology reports total_raw_records, unique_before_limit, unique_records, and duplicates_removed
Records without abstracts were excluded from analytical extraction or clearly labeled metadata-only
DOI, arXiv, OpenAlex identifiers, provenance, and conflicts were preserved through extraction
Published and preprint versions merged by ScholarFlow were cited once using the canonical published DOI form
If the ScholarFlow tool was unavailable, the agent disclosed that all-index coverage could not be met before offering the arXiv fallback

evals.prompt: Use the supplied page-numbered full text to check every quotation in a 5-paper APA literature survey, and tell me which conclusions the papers prove.
evals.expected_output: A literature survey that uses page-level quote location where available while refusing to equate textual presence with semantic claim support.
expectations: The skill read SKILL.md for systematic-literature-review
The agent called scholarflow-academic_assess_claim_evidence once when a judge was configured, or scholarflow-academic_verify_evidence_spans once when it was not
The methodology reported located, quote_not_found, and page_missing outcomes without hiding failures
The report stated that quote location verifies textual presence and page coordinates only
The agent did not claim conclusions were proved solely because a quote was located or a model returned supported
When semantic assessment ran, the report preserved model, confidence, labels, and cited span IDs; otherwise it preserved semantic_support as not_assessed

evals.prompt: I uploaded PDFs for a 6-paper review. Extract their page text, check the exact quotations, and classify each major claim as supported, contradicted, or insufficient. Explain what the score means.
evals.expected_output: A page-traceable review that uses bounded PDF extraction and structured model judging while disclosing extraction and evaluation boundaries.
expectations: The skill read SKILL.md for systematic-literature-review
The agent used scholarflow-academic_extract_pdf_pages only with caller-supplied PDF bytes and did not ask it to fetch URLs or arbitrary paths
The report disclosed truncated or empty pages and stated that OCR and layout reconstruction were not performed
The agent called scholarflow-academic_assess_claim_evidence once rather than redundantly calling the quote locator first
Only page-located quotes were submitted for semantic classification
Supported and contradicted verdicts cited supplied span IDs and preserved judge model, request, and confidence metadata
The report described verdicts as model judgements over supplied evidence rather than scientific truth
Any reported macro-F1 was tied to a named gold dataset and described as oracle-evidence classification rather than retrieval quality
